## Goal

As an operator I need a **measured, reproducible verdict** on whether
`/sys/class/drm/card0/device/gpu_metrics` (the `amd_gpu_metrics_v3_0` blob, the
interface `amdgpu_top` reads) carries a *graded* GFX-activity signal on this
Strix Halo APU — one that separates compute from idle the way the
power-derived `gpu:computing:bool` rule does but `gpu_busy_percent` does not —
and, only if such a field passes an explicit discrimination bar, to have it
published as a Prometheus series through the existing 10 s textfile sampler.
A negative verdict, recorded with numbers so the path is never retried, is an
equally valid outcome.

## Problem statement

The usage report's GPU busy time infers activity from power draw
(`gpu:computing:bool >= bool 90`), which cannot tell GFX work from any other
power draw. `gpu_busy_percent` was eliminated as a utilisation signal
(2026-10-28: 45.2 % false-busy, Pearson r = 0.28 against power,
LP-0MVSQQO910077LYL), leaving `gpu_metrics` as the last candidate hardware
activity source. **Intake measurements (2026-10-29) show that candidate is very
probably dead too**: `average_gfx_activity` read **100 % on every one of 120
samples across two captures** while package power moved between 42 W and 123 W
and DRAM bandwidth between 0.7 and 59.5 GB/s. This item therefore exists to
settle the question with evidence and a stated bar, not to assume the answer.

## Users

- **Operator (primary).** "Is the GPU actually doing work right now, and was it
  busy between 17:00 and 19:00?" — needs a utilisation figure that is a direct
  measurement, not a power-draw proxy.
- **Agent answering a usage/incident question (secondary).** Needs to know which
  hardware fields are trustworthy on this host so it cites a real signal instead
  of re-litigating `gpu_busy_percent`.

User stories:

- As an operator I can run one command that decodes `gpu_metrics`, samples it
  alongside power and `gpu_busy_percent`, and prints per-field discrimination
  statistics — so the verdict rests on numbers I can reproduce.
- As an operator I am told plainly whether the interface gives a graded signal,
  with the capture date, kernel, sample counts and band means, so I never
  re-investigate it.
- As an operator, if a field does pass, the series appears next to the existing
  `gpu_*` textfile series without a new daemon, port or scrape job.

## Existing state (measured during intake, 2026-10-29, kernel 7.0.0-34-generic)

| Question | Evidence |
|---|---|
| Is the file live and readable? | `-r--r--r-- 4096` root:root; 264 bytes of content; values change between reads; no root, no ROCm, no `amd-smi` needed |
| Which structure? | Header decodes to `structure_size=264, format_revision=3, content_revision=0` → `struct gpu_metrics_v3_0` (`drivers/gpu/drm/amd/include/kgd_pp_interface.h`; the same header text is vendored in `libdrm_amdgpu_sys`'s `wrapper_gpu_metrics.h`) |
| Does the layout check out? | Field sizes under `#pragma pack(4)` sum to 260 B; 4 B tail padding = **264 B**, matching `structure_size` exactly. Cross-checks: `average_socket_power` 95 060 mW vs hwmon `power1_average` 95.06 W (0.1 % agreement); `average_gfx_power` 11.3–44.2 W; `average_gfxclk_frequency` 2 711–2 900 MHz; `average_dram_reads` 0.7–59.5 GB/s; `average_vcn_activity` 0; `average_ipu_activity` all 0; `temperature_gfx` 56–69 °C |
| Does the activity field discriminate? | **No.** Capture A (60 samples @1 s): power 44–123 W, DRAM 1.8–59.5 GB/s → `average_gfx_activity` = 100 on all 60. Capture B (60 samples @1 s): power 42–66 W (idle band), DRAM 0.7–3.5 GB/s → 100 on all 60. Spot samples earlier: 97, 99, 100 at 41–57 W |
| How does it compare with the rejected counter? | Identically saturated: `gpu_busy_percent` = 100 on all 120 samples of both captures; `rocm-smi --showuse` reports `GPU use 100 %` at 54 W. GFX clock is pinned at its 2 900 MHz maximum in *both* bands, so the GFX domain is never gated while the proxy holds the device |
| What *does* vary with load? | `average_dram_reads`/`average_dram_writes` (memory bandwidth, 0.7 → 59.5 GB/s), `average_gfx_power` (11.3 → 44.2 W), `average_socket_power` (42 → 123 W), `average_core_c0_activity` (per-core C0 residency) |
| Are the values instantaneous? | No — they are SMU **time filtered** (`time_filter_alphavalue` = 1 000 000); the filter window is undocumented, so no claim finer than the sample interval is supportable |

Existing pipeline this would plug into: `gpu-metrics.service` runs
`~/.local/bin/gpu-metrics-textfile.sh` every 10 s, writing `gpu.prom` into
node_exporter's textfile collector (`gpu_busy_percent`, `gpu_vram_*`,
`gpu_gtt_used_bytes`, label `gpu="card0"`), scraped every 15 s by Prometheus;
documented in [docs/systemd/gpu-metrics.service](../../docs/systemd/gpu-metrics.service)
and [monitoring/README.md](../../monitoring/README.md).

## Desired change

1. **A reproducible probe CLI** — `scripts/gpu_metrics_probe.py`: decode the
   v3.0 blob from a sysfs path (default
   `/sys/class/drm/card0/device/gpu_metrics`), sample every candidate activity
   field alongside the two reference signals (amdgpu hwmon `power1_average` and
   `gpu_busy_percent`) at a configurable interval for a configurable duration,
   and emit CSV or `--json`. A `--verdict` mode prints the per-field
   discrimination statistics against the bar below.
2. **A recorded verdict** — the measured numbers plus a pass/fail decision per
   candidate field, written into the work item and the two monitoring documents,
   so the interface is either adopted once or closed off permanently.
3. **Conditional publication** — only if a field passes the bar, publish it
   through the existing 10 s textfile sampler (new `# HELP`/`# TYPE` series with
   the `gpu="card0"` label, atomic write, nothing written on read failure). If
   nothing passes, publish nothing and record why.
4. **A regression guard** — a saturated activity field must not be usable as a
   utilisation input in any rule or report query without a test failing.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `scripts/gpu_metrics_probe.py` decodes `gpu_metrics` into named fields
  using the pinned v3.0 layout and validates the header
  (`structure_size` == layout size, `format_revision` == 3); unit tests cover a
  real 264-byte capture committed as a fixture, a truncated buffer, and an
  unknown `format_revision`/`structure_size`, which must be rejected with a
  clear error rather than misparsed.
- [ ] A capture (`--duration`/`--interval`, defaults documented) writes one row
  per sample containing a timestamp, every candidate activity field,
  `power1_average_watts` and `gpu_busy_percent`; a test drives the sampler
  against fixture sysfs trees (fake `/sys/class/drm/card0/device` and hwmon
  directory) and asserts row count, monotonic timestamps and fixture-derived
  values, without sleeping.
- [ ] `--verdict` reports, per candidate field, the idle-band mean (< 60 W), the
  compute-band mean (≥ 90 W), their separation in percentage points, Pearson r
  against package power, and the idle-band false-busy share (samples ≥ 90 %
  while power < 60 W); a field passes only if separation ≥ 30 pp **and**
  r ≥ 0.6 **and** idle-band false-busy ≤ 10 %. Unit tests drive synthetic
  saturated, graded and noisy series and assert the exact pass/fail decision and
  the printed statistics.
- [ ] The measured numbers and the resulting verdict — positive **or** negative
  — are recorded in `docs/systemd/gpu-metrics.service`,
  `monitoring/README.md` (the "Why not `amd-smi`, `rocm-smi` or `amdtop`?"
  section gains a `gpu_metrics` row) and the work item, including capture date,
  kernel version, sample counts and band statistics; a negative verdict is a
  complete outcome, not a failure.
- [ ] If a field passed, the 10 s textfile sampler publishes it (series name,
  `# HELP`/`# TYPE`, `gpu="card0"` label) with the existing atomic-write and
  write-nothing-on-failure behaviour, and `docs/systemd/gpu-metrics.service`
  documents the series and its meaning; a test runs the sampler against fixture
  sysfs and asserts its emitted series set exactly matches the set the
  documentation table lists (so docs and behaviour cannot drift). If no field
  passed, no new series is added and the test asserts the sampler's series set is
  unchanged.
- [ ] The pinned-counter guard in `proxy/tests/test_monitoring_deployment.py`
  (`FORBIDDEN_RULE_SERIES`) is extended so a saturated activity field cannot
  appear as a utilisation input — `gpu_busy_percent` always, and the
  `gpu_metrics` activity fields when the verdict is negative — with a regression
  test that fails if any `monitoring/*.yaml` rule expression or the probe's own
  utilisation expressions select one.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
  comments, docstrings, `docs/systemd/gpu-metrics.service` and
  `monitoring/README.md`; the probe's re-measure procedure (how to re-run the
  capture after a kernel, firmware or driver change) is documented.
- [ ] Full project test suite passes with the new changes via `/skill:test`.

## Constraints

- **No new daemon, port or scrape job.** Reuse `gpu-metrics.service` →
  node_exporter textfile collector; the sampler's 10 s cadence and Prometheus's
  15 s scrape interval are the resolution floor and must be stated as such.
- **Host state is part of the deliverable.** The sampler script lives in
  `~/.local/bin/gpu-metrics-textfile.sh` and is documented in
  `docs/systemd/gpu-metrics.service`; any change to its series must be reflected
  there so a clean clone can reproduce it.
- **Repository boundary.** `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/` (`gpu_busy.py`,
  `reporting.py`) is not edited — adopting a passing field in the daily report is
  a follow-up item, mirroring the constraint recorded in LP-0MVNWUEY8008XM6W.
- **The layout must be pinned in-repo.** The struct is not shipped in the
  installed `linux-headers` packages on this host, so the field table must be
  transcribed with a cited source (`struct gpu_metrics_v3_0`) and validated
  against the observed 264-byte `structure_size`; it must fail closed when the
  kernel reports a different revision.
- **No instantaneous claims.** The values are SMU time-filtered with an
  undocumented window; the output must say so rather than imply per-second
  fidelity.
- **Read cost.** One 264-byte sysfs read per sample; world-readable, no root, no
  ROCm userspace, no `amd-smi`.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `scripts/gpu_metrics_probe.py` — New. v3.0 decoder (field table + header
  validation), paired sampler for `gpu_metrics` + hwmon power + `gpu_busy_percent`,
  band statistics and the pass/fail verdict; CSV and `--json` output.
- `tests/test_gpu_metrics_probe.py` — New. Decoder fixtures (real 264-byte
  capture, truncated, unknown revision), fixture-sysfs sampling, verdict
  arithmetic and boundary cases (power exactly 60 W / 90 W, activity exactly
  90 %).
- `tests/fixtures/gpu_metrics_v3_0.bin` — New. One committed real capture so the
  layout assertion is reproducible.
- `docs/systemd/gpu-metrics.service` — Record the verdict, the decode layout and
  (conditionally) the new series; extend the verification section with the probe
  command.
- `monitoring/README.md` — Add `gpu_metrics` to "Why not `amd-smi`, `rocm-smi`
  or `amdtop`?" with the measured band statistics; note the re-measure recipe.
- `monitoring/gpu_compute_rules.yaml` — Header comment records the `gpu_metrics`
  verdict (no rule change expected; the power rule stays authoritative).
- `proxy/tests/test_monitoring_deployment.py` — Extend `FORBIDDEN_RULE_SERIES`
  so saturated activity fields are rejected as utilisation inputs.
- `~/.local/bin/gpu-metrics-textfile.sh` — Only if a field passed: emit the new
  series from the same atomic write.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Risk: the premise is false.** Intake evidence already shows
  `average_gfx_activity` saturated at 100 % from 42 W to 123 W. Mitigation: the
  negative verdict is an explicit, accepted outcome (AC4) and the probe records
  which fields *do* discriminate (DRAM bandwidth, GFX power) for a follow-up.
- **Risk: decoder drift after a kernel or firmware upgrade.** Mitigation: header
  validation plus a committed real capture; the probe refuses unknown revisions
  and the docs carry the re-measure procedure.
- **Risk: undocumented APU field semantics.** `average_gfx_activity` may mean
  "GFX domain powered" rather than "GFX busy" on SMU 14. Mitigation: the bar and
  band statistics decide it, and the interpretation limits are documented.
- **Risk: a capture that misses one band.** A verdict computed only from idle
  samples would be meaningless. Mitigation: AC3 requires both bands, and the
  probe reports per-band sample counts so a one-sided capture is visible.
- **Risk: scope creep** into report integration, new daemons or a full GPU
  telemetry redesign. Mitigation: those are explicit constraints/follow-ups, not
  scope.
- **Assumption:** amdgpu hwmon `power1_average` remains the reference compute
  signal (idle ≈ 40–54 W, computing ≈ 115 W, threshold 90 W) per
  LP-0MVO8DOHP008FL48; this item does not re-derive the threshold.
- **Assumption:** the discrimination bar (≥ 30 pp separation, r ≥ 0.6, ≤ 10 %
  idle false-busy) is strict enough — it is far stricter than
  `gpu_busy_percent`'s measured 45.2 % false-busy — and is recorded here so the
  producer can tighten or relax it before implementation.
- **Assumption:** both bands occur on this host within a short window (intake saw
  idle at 42–66 W and compute at 90–123 W within ~15 minutes), so a 30-minute
  capture is sufficient; longer captures are supported by the same CLI.
- **Assumption:** priority stays `high` — the verdict decides whether a direct
  hardware utilisation measure is possible at all on this host, which the usage
  report's honesty goal depends on — even though the likely outcome is a short
  negative report rather than a code change.

## Related work

- **LP-0MVSQQO910077LYL** — Evaluate `amd-smi` as the GPU utilisation source
  (completed). Quantified `gpu_busy_percent`'s saturation (45.2 % false-busy,
  r = 0.28) and filed this item as the remaining avenue. Parent context.
- **LP-0MVNWUEY8008XM6W** — Add GPU telemetry sampler for true utilisation
  history (in review). Owns the *workload* half (per-slot busy/idle, in-flight
  tasks, the `gpu_utilisation.py` CLI). **Partial overlap only**: that item
  attributes power to llama-server slots; this one judges a *hardware* activity
  field. No CLI or slot work is duplicated here — this item produces a probe and
  a verdict, and its publication step (if any) extends the existing sysfs
  sampler.
- **LP-0MVO8CLCL00086NT** — Monitoring: deployable, tailnet-exposed Prometheus
  with honest GPU utilisation (completed) and children: LP-0MVO8DOHP008FL48
  (power-derived utilisation rules), LP-0MVO8DORX004P05G (docs for the deployed
  stack). The sampler, units and docs this item extends.
- **LP-0MS9GA6QL007XTBP** — Fix GPU-wedge false positives (completed):
  established that `gpu_busy_percent` is unusable and power is the
  discriminating signal; the proxy's wedge detector was disabled because of it.
- **LP-0MVOHRLPB0086Q5T** — Grafana dashboard GPU VRAM panel queries series no
  exporter publishes (in progress): the precedent for asserting *published*
  series against documentation, which AC5 reuses.
- **LP-0MVNWULLI006ZYXX** — Cross-check report slot-time against llama-server
  eval timings (independent): the other half of validating the report's busy
  figures.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No interactive operator was available for this intake (auto-dispatched by the
herdr downtime worker at 2026-10-29T03:54:28Z), so each question below was
resolved from host and repository evidence; none is blocking. Each carries the
agent's **Recommended** option, which the producer may override.

- **Q1: Given that `average_gfx_activity` already measures as saturated (100 %
  from 42 W to 123 W), is a documented negative verdict an acceptable
  deliverable for this item?**
  **Recommended:** yes — record the numbers, close the path permanently, and file
  follow-ups for the fields that do discriminate.
  — Answer (research, 2026-10-29): the item was written to test the hypothesis,
  not to assume it; the file decodes correctly (264 B v3.0, cross-checked
  against hwmon power) yet its activity field does not respond to load, so the
  honest outcome is a negative verdict with evidence. Source: two 60-sample 1 s
  captures (power 44–123 W and 42–66 W, DRAM 0.7–59.5 GB/s, activity 100 on all
  120 samples), `/tmp` probe using the `kgd_pp_interface.h` v3.0 layout.
- **Q2: If a field does pass the bar, should it replace the power-derived
  `gpu:computing:bool` as the report's GPU busy measure, or be published
  alongside it?**
  **Recommended:** publish alongside; keep power-derived authoritative until its
  own calibration item justifies switching.
  — Answer (research, 2026-10-29): `gpu:computing:bool` is referenced by the
  report (`gpu_busy.py`, `reporting.py`), the alert `GpuComputingSustained` and
  `monitoring/tests/gpu_rules_test.yml`; changing its meaning inside an
  investigation item would break three consumers at once. Publishing an additive
  series keeps the comparison visible, and report adoption stays a follow-up
  (same boundary recorded in LP-0MVNWUEY8008XM6W). Source:
  `monitoring/gpu_compute_rules.yaml`, `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/scripts/gpu_busy.py`.
- **Q3: Where should the probe live, and how should a passing field reach
  Prometheus — extend the deployed bash textfile sampler, or add a Python
  sampler?**
  **Recommended:** a repo `scripts/gpu_metrics_probe.py` decoder plus a one-line
  call from the existing bash sampler; no new unit.
  — Answer (research, 2026-10-29): the sampler is a documented 10 s bash loop
  writing `gpu.prom` atomically, and `docs/systemd/gpu-metrics.service` embeds
  the script verbatim; a second sampler would duplicate the unit, the textfile
  directory and the docs. Decoding a 264-byte binary blob in bash is not
  testable, so the field table belongs in Python with fixture tests. Source:
  `docs/systemd/gpu-metrics.service`, `~/.local/bin/gpu-metrics-textfile.sh`.

## Goal (user story)

As an operator, I want each `slot_ratio_seed` line to carry the snapshot path it
resolved (or the candidate paths it tried) and whether the sidecar was present,
so the remaining per-session cause of `missing_sidecar` / `missing_snapshot` is
attributable from logs instead of inferred from code inspection.

## Why (evidence)

The verdict on LP-0MVK0E8C40035FG3 (docs/dev/slot-ratio-seed-verdict-LP-0MVK0E8C40035FG3.md)
proved from 4,488 decisions that the seed path always fails at the lookup
(`missing_sidecar` 75.8 %, `missing_snapshot` 24.2 %; `found`, `expired`,
`prefix_mismatch` all 0). It identified two provable writer-side gaps (the
eviction save path writes no sidecar; the request path skips the sidecar when no
usage block was measured) but could not split the 31 affected sessions between
them, because `missing_sidecar` records `stored_messages=0` by design and logs
neither the resolved `slot_<session>.bin` path nor the sidecar path.

## Scope

**In scope:** one extra field on the existing INFO line (behaviour-neutral) plus
tests/docs. **Out of scope:** any change to the credit decision, `prefix_matches`,
the TTL, or the sidecar format (those belong to LP-0MVJXV0MY000O77E).

## Proposed change

1. In `proxy/proxy/slot_cache_ratio.py`, extend `log_seed_outcome()` with an
   optional `slot=<basename>` field (basename only — no absolute paths in logs)
   and pass the resolved candidate for `missing_sidecar` / `missing_snapshot`,
   so a later grep can tell which directory/endpoint variant resolved.
2. Cover every outcome branch in `proxy/tests/test_slot_cache_ratio_restore.py`.
3. Document the extra field in `proxy/docs/routing.md`.

## Acceptance criteria

- Every `slot_ratio_seed` line names the resolved snapshot basename (or the
  first candidate tried when none exists), covered by a unit test per branch.
- No behaviour change: the existing outcome vocabulary and credit decision are
  untouched, and the full seed-outcome test suite passes.
- `proxy/docs/routing.md` documents the field.

## Traceability

- discovered-from: LP-0MVK0E8C40035FG3 (verdict could not split the
  `missing_sidecar` sub-causes from logs)

## Goal

As the proxy operator I want one INFO log line per compaction-header emission
(and one distinguishable line when compaction was evaluated but emitted
nothing), so that reading the proxy log tells me whether the signal was
emitted at all — closing secondary finding 2 of the parent ("Header emission
logs nothing ... a loaded-but-idle extension is indistinguishable from a broken
one") and satisfying AC4's proxy half.

Parent: LP-0MVWBFN8L004Z3X8. Unconditional — this is required whether or not
Phase A/B pass.

## Current state (verified during planning)

- `proxy/proxy/router.py:397` `_build_compaction_headers()` returns `{}` or the
  header dict; the only log statement in it is
  `logger.debug("Failed to build compaction headers; omitting", ...)` on the
  exception path (`router.py:430`). The success path logs nothing.
- `router.py:2336` applies it with `outgoing_headers.update(...)` on the
  streaming path; a second site near `router.py:3551` covers the buffered path.
- `router_helpers.py:6218` already logs `session_compaction applied
  session=… priority=… est_before=… est_after=…` — but that line proves
  *compaction happened*, not that *headers were emitted*. The two can diverge
  (e.g. `compaction_summary_text` empty → no headers, compaction still
  applied).

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: On the live-applied path, exactly one INFO line per response is logged:
  `compaction_headers emitted session=<id8> turns_summarized=<n>
  recent_turns_kept=<k> marker_chars=<len>`. It is logged once per response on
  both the streaming (SSE) and buffered response paths — never once per SSE
  chunk.
- AC2: A response that evaluated compaction but emitted no headers logs exactly
  one line naming the reason, distinguishable from "emitted": one of
  `compaction_headers none reason=disabled|below_trigger|noop|dry_run|
  remote_with_guidance|no_summary_text|build_failed`. `no_summary_text` covers
  the real divergence case (compaction applied, summary missing) and
  `build_failed` covers the exception path.
- AC3: No header-emission line is emitted for requests that never reach the
  compaction path (e.g. remote dispatch with no session), keeping router log
  volume unchanged for the overwhelmingly common `compaction_disabled` case at
  a rate that permits long-window analysis (the `session_compaction applied`
  line already fires per compacted request; the new line must not multiply
  log volume for non-compaction traffic).
- AC4: The fail-safe contract is unchanged and better observed: an exception
  while building headers still yields no headers and never changes dispatch,
  but is now logged at **WARNING** with `exc_info=True` (was `debug`), so a
  silently broken emission is visible in normal operation.
- AC5: Header names, values and encodings are untouched:
  `proxy/tests/test_compaction_headers_contract.py` passes **unmodified**.
- AC6: Unit tests assert: the AC1 line and each field on both response paths;
  exactly one AC1 line per response with a multi-chunk SSE stream; the AC2
  reason line for `disabled` / `below_trigger` / `dry_run` /
  `remote_with_guidance` / `no_summary_text`; WARNING + `exc_info` on the
  exception path; and that a logging failure cannot raise out of the emission
  path (fail-safe preserved).
- AC7: No marker text, no summary body and no message content appear in any
  log line — only ids, counts and lengths.
- (Parent AC4) the proxy logs one INFO per header emission (session, `turns_summarized`, `recent_turns_kept`, marker length) and the bridge logs one line per signal capture and one per reshape. A reader of the logs can tell "no signal emitted" from "signal emitted, bridge ignored it".

## Minimal Implementation

- Add a module-level helper in `proxy/proxy/router.py` next to
  `_build_compaction_headers` — e.g. `_log_compaction_headers(session_id,
  headers, reason=None)` — and call it from the two `outgoing_headers.update(
  _build_compaction_headers(...))` sites, so the accounting is in one place
  and both paths are testable with the existing `_mock_upstream_response`
  fixtures.
- Derive `reason` where the decision is already known rather than re-deriving
  it: `_build_compaction_headers` can return `(headers, reason)` internally
  while keeping its public single-dict behaviour, or the caller can read
  `session_result["compaction_reason"]` / `compaction_applied`. Prefer the
  minimal change that does not alter the contract test's public seam.
- Session id is already available at both call sites (`session_id`); truncate
  to 8 chars like the existing `session_compaction applied` line does, so
  operator greps work across both lines.
- `marker_chars` is `len(marker_b64)` (the header value length), which is what
  the parent's AC4 asks for ("marker length").

## Deliverables

- Emission telemetry in `proxy/proxy/router.py` on both response paths.
- Unit tests in `proxy/tests/test_compaction_headers_contract.py` (extend) or
  a new `proxy/tests/test_compaction_headers_telemetry.py` (preferred: keeps the
  frozen contract file untouched per AC5).

**Key Files:**

- `proxy/proxy/router.py`
- `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py`
- `proxy/tests/test_compaction_headers_contract.py`
- `proxy/tests/test_compaction_headers_telemetry.py`
- `docs/session-compaction-design.md`

## Dependencies

None. Required by the T1 execution child (its pass criteria C/D are read from
these lines) and by the parent's AC4.

  with `--reason "Not needed: Phase A and Phase B both PASS (<verdict links>);
  AC5 remains unmet by design because no divergence was observed"` and change
  no code.
- Otherwise implement exactly the failing link. Phase A fail ⇒ the producer
  contract is the defect (no base id is meaningful yet; fix the link named on
  the T1 child and re-run T1 instead of building the handshake). Phase B fail
  with a recorded fail signature ⇒ implement the handshake below.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: The proxy emits `X-Compaction-Base-Id` with the compaction header set:
  a stable hash (SHA-256, first 16 hex chars) of the **exact** compacted message
  list it dispatched; the same list always yields the same id and any change to
  roles, order or content changes it. The hash input/serialisation is
  documented in a docstring so the client can reproduce it.
- AC2: The proxy accepts `X-Dispatch-Base-Id` on the request. On a match it
  adopts the client's base instead of re-summarising (no CREATION
  re-summarisation) and logs
  `compaction_base adopt session=<id8> base=<id8>` at INFO.
- AC3: On a mismatch the proxy logs one WARNING naming both ids
  (`compaction_base mismatch session=<id8> proxy_base=<id8>
  client_base=<id8>`), re-signals once (emits the header set again on that
  response), and does **not** report `history_mismatch` for this cause.
- AC4: A second consecutive divergence for the same session stops mirroring for
  that session and logs the reason at WARNING
  (`compaction_base mirroring_off session=<id8> reason=second_divergence`);
  subsequent responses for that session carry no `X-Compaction-*` headers, so
  the client cannot loop.
- AC5: Clients that send no `X-Dispatch-Base-Id` behave exactly as today
  (contract preserved; `proxy/tests/test_compaction_headers_contract.py` green
  unmodified) — the handshake is additive and opt-in on the client side.
- AC6: No payload content, marker text or summary body appears in any log line
  or header beyond the existing base64 marker — only ids and counts.
- AC7: Unit tests cover: hash determinism and sensitivity (reordered turns,
  changed content, changed role); adopt-on-match (no summariser call — asserted
  with a summariser spy); single-mismatch re-signal (exactly one extra emission);
  second-divergence mirroring-off; absent-client-header passthrough; and that a
  malformed/truncated base id is treated as absent, not as a mismatch.
- AC8: The bridge (SorraAgents) sends `X-Dispatch-Base-Id` when it has captured
  a signal, and clears it when it clears state; its unit tests extend to cover
  send/clear. Recorded with the SorraAgents commit hash on this item.
- (Parent AC5) if the mirrored base diverges, the proxy detects it explicitly (base id mismatch, logged) instead of reporting `history_mismatch`, and re-signals exactly once; a second consecutive divergence stops mirroring for that session and logs why.

## Minimal Implementation

- Producer: compute the base id once, where the compacted list is built
  (`router_helpers.py` live-applied path), carry it on the session result
  alongside `compaction_summary_text`, and add it to
  `_build_compaction_headers`. Mismatch handling lives where the session store
  is compared (`session_manager.py` / `session.py`), reusing the existing
  `fallback_reason` plumbing rather than adding a second path.
- Client: reuse the existing per-session state map — store the id with the
  signal, add it to the outgoing header set in the dispatch path; no new
  persistence.
- Keep the "re-signal exactly once" counter in the existing per-session store,
  not in a new global.

## Deliverables

- Base-id emission + adoption/mismatch handling with unit tests.
- Bridge dispatch-header plumbing + tests.
- A paragraph in `docs/session-compaction-design.md` §7.3 describing the
  handshake and its stop condition.

**Key Files:**

- `proxy/proxy/router.py`
- `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py`
- `proxy/proxy/session_manager.py`
- `proxy/proxy/session.py`
- `proxy/tests/test_compaction_headers_contract.py`
- `pi-client/proxy-compaction-bridge/compaction-bridge.js`

Depends on the T2 execution child (its verdict is this child's gate).

## Finding

The proxy's log retention (7 days: `logging.retention_days` default in
`proxy/proxy/utils.py:1034`, which makes `TimedRotatingFileHandler` keep
`backupCount = 7 × 24 / 6 = 28` six-hour segments, with `/etc/logrotate.d/llama-proxy`
as a `rotate 7` daily safety net) is shorter than the age a committed
measurement record reaches before it is audited or re-examined.

Concrete instance: `LP-0MVV29XDW006VTWK` had to restate the pre-change baseline
on the window `2026-10-28 00:10:18` → `2026-10-29 00:10:18` (8 days before the
implementing session). The window was measured in full on 2026-10-30, but by
2026-11-05 the first ~16 h of `2026-10-28` had been pruned: only
`proxy.log.2026-10-28_16.gz` (16:16:14→22:16:12) and
`proxy.log.2026-10-29_001015.gz` (00:00:00→00:10:15) survive — **6 h 10 m of a
24 h window (25.7 %, 67 of 136 enqueued waits)**. The committed record
therefore carries two provenance classes (measurement-time full window vs
today's coverage re-measurement) instead of a single regenerable artefact.

This is a recurring shape, not a one-off: any "measure a window, then commit a
record" slice that lands more than ~7 days after its window has to be
documented as un-reproducible, and every AC of the form "re-running the
embedded command regenerates the committed JSON" degrades to "regenerable
while the archives survive".

## Goal (user story)

As the LLM proxy operator, I want a measurement window to stay re-derivable for
at least as long as the records that quote it, so a committed record can be
re-checked by a later session instead of being taken on trust.

## Options (not a decision — intake should choose)

1. **Raise `logging.retention_days`** (e.g. 7→14 or 30). Cheap in disk: measured
   on 2026-11-05, `/var/log/llama-proxy` holds 46 `proxy.log*.gz` archives
   totalling **42 MB** (≈0.9 MB per six-hour segment), so doubling or
   quadrupling retention costs tens of MB, not GB. The knob already exists
   (`logging.retention_days`). Costs: more files in one directory (check
   `prune_logs` startup scan time) and the logrotate drop-in's `rotate 7`
   safety net must be raised to match, or it will prune what the in-process
   handler retains.
2. **Archive the window's archives with the record** — a `--emit-archives`
   mode or a documented `tar`/`rsync` step alongside a record commit. Larger
   repo footprint (or an external artefact store), but makes the record
   self-contained forever.
3. **Record the harness output as the artefact of authority** and drop the
   "regenerates byte-for-byte" expectation from records older than retention —
   documentation-only, no code change; what `LP-0MVV29XDW006VTWK` does today.

## Acceptance criteria (draft, for intake)

- AC1: A documented retention window is at least as long as the longest-lived
  measurement record the project commits, with the value stated in
  `docs/dev/` and pinned by a test.
- AC2: A measurement record older than the retention window is either
  reproducible from a committed/archived artefact, or the record states its
  provenance classes explicitly (no silent re-derivation claim).
- AC3: Disk cost of the chosen retention is measured, not assumed, and stated
  on the host-install/retention doc.

## Evidence

- `docs/dev/prefill-admission-conversion-diurnal-baseline.md`
  ("Provenance and coverage") — the coverage map and the pruning mechanism.
- `proxy/proxy/utils.py` (`setup_logging`, `prune_logs`,
  `logging.retention_days` default 7).
- `/etc/logrotate.d/llama-proxy` (`rotate 7`, `size`-free daily safety net).
- `scripts/lib/proxy_logs.py` — rotation/decompression discovery (unaffected;
  the loss is retention, not discovery).

# Intake Brief: Improve the Web UI Prompt Log

## Headline

Make the `/logs` **Prompt Log** tab readable and more useful: show the *text* of the first message (not the dumped Python repr of its content-block list), and add a second **Current message** column showing the text of the request's last message.

## Problem statement

The Prompt Log tab records one entry per handled request and displays the request's first non-system message in a `Prompt (first non-system message)` column. For any client that sends structured content — which is *all* agent traffic, i.e. almost every entry — `proxy.prompt_log.extract_prompt()` reduces the message to `str(content)` of a content-block list, so the column renders a Python/JSON repr instead of prose:

```
[{'type': 'text', 'text': 'Do we have a work item that will improve logging in the web UI?'}]
```

Measured on the local `prompt-log.jsonl*` (≈114.5 K entries, 2026-11-17): **114 424** entries are repr'd block lists; only ~58 are plain text. The operator therefore has to decode a data structure to read a sentence — and the tab also only ever shows the *opening* prompt of a session, never what was actually just submitted.

## Users

**Primary:** the operator/LLM-proxy maintainer who uses the `/logs` page to audit and triage proxy traffic (which sessions are running, what they were asked, what was most recently asked).

**User stories:**

- "As an operator, I want the Prompt column to show the message *text*, so I can read what a session was asked without parsing a Python list."
- "As an operator, I want a second column with the message just submitted, so I can see the current turn of a long-running agent session rather than only its opening prompt."
- "As an operator, I want non-text payloads (images, tool results) marked explicitly instead of silently dropped, so I can tell a text-free request from an empty one — and I accept that entries recorded before this change keep their raw display rather than being rewritten."

## Existing state (verified in this checkout, `dev`)

- **Writer** — `proxy/proxy/prompt_log.py`: `record_exchange()` is hooked from `proxy.ui.proxy_openai_api`, resolves the session ID, requested model and routed model (`X-Resolved-Model` → `X-Provider` → `error:<code>`), and appends exactly one complete JSONL line per handled request. Bounded and non-fatal by contract: capped `prompt` (`prompt_log.max_prompt_chars`, default 2000, with a `truncated` flag), bounded tail read (`max_entries`, default 500), rotation to `prompt-log.jsonl.N` (`max_file_bytes`, `max_rotated_files`), daemon writer thread, counted `write_errors`/`dropped`, rate-limited error logging.
- **Extraction** — `extract_prompt()` returns `str(content)` via `router_helpers._first_message_content()` (first message whose `role != "system"`; `prompt` field for `/v1/completions`). `_first_message_content()` is **shared** with the `proxy.log` body preview (`_get_request_preview`, 80-char cap), so changing it in place would also change the existing log-preview behaviour.
- **Reader/API** — `recent_payload()` → `GET /logs/prompt-log` returns `{enabled, entries(newest-first), counters, max_entries, file}`; `recent_entries()` reads a bounded tail, newest first, and spans rotated files.
- **UI** — `proxy/templates/view_logs.html`: the Prompt Log tab (third tab, `switchTab('prompt')`) polls the endpoint every 5 s while visible and renders a table with columns **Time | Session | Routed model | Prompt (first non-system message)**; previews are capped at `PROMPT_PREVIEW_CHARS = 240` with a `…` marker and the full value in the `title` tooltip; all values pass through `escapeHtml()`.
- **Tests** — `proxy/tests/test_prompt_log.py` (25 tests: entry shape, session-ID chain, completions, routed-model resolution, truncation, disabled mode, append/rotation/read failures, config resolution/validation, endpoint shape, `/logs` page renders the tab). Playwright specs live alongside (`slot-logs.spec.js`, `status-bar.spec.js`, …).
- **Existing precedent** — `session_recorder._extract_message_text()` already flattens a content-block list into its `type: "text"` parts (used by the `/logs` session-dropdown preview, LP-0MRAZPRF6008537P) but it only handles the `text` type, only the first `role: "user"` message, and returns nothing for non-text blocks — it is a starting point to generalise rather than a drop-in.
- **Docs** — `proxy/README.md` § *Prompt Log (`prompt-log.jsonl`)* documents the field table and the tab; `README.md` line 45 summarises it.
- **Data reality** — of the repr'd entries sampled, 25 388 parse with `ast.literal_eval` (all `type: "text"` blocks) and 15 787 do **not** (truncated mid-block by `max_prompt_chars`). Recorded as evidence of the extent only: per D2, existing entries are **not** decoded or migrated — the fix applies to entries recorded from now on.

## Desired change

1. **First-message column shows text.** When a message's `content` is a list of content blocks, concatenate the `text` of its text parts (`type: "text"`, and `input_text` where present) instead of `str()`-ing the list. Plain-string content is unchanged.
2. **Second column: current message.** Add a `Current message` column showing the readable text of the request's **last non-system** message, labelled with that message's role, so an operator sees the turn in flight rather than only the session opener.
3. **Record the new field** in the JSONL (so the file itself stays the source of truth and stays greppable), keeping the existing `prompt` field's meaning intact for backwards compatibility.
4. **Entries already on disk are left alone.** No read-time decoding, no repr parsing and no file migration: the tab becomes readable for entries recorded after this change, while older rows keep today's raw display until they age out of the window/rotation.

## Implementation plan (ordered; test-first where practical)

1. **Test-first: pure helpers in `proxy/proxy/prompt_log.py`.** Write the failing tests in `proxy/tests/test_prompt_log.py` for two new helpers — `flatten_message_content(content)` (a string passes through unchanged; a block list concatenates its `text`/`input_text` parts; each non-text block becomes a short placeholder such as `<image>` / `<tool_result:1234 chars>`; empty/no-text content yields a single placeholder or `""` as specified) and `extract_last_non_system_message(body_json)` returning `(text, role)` while skipping any `role == "system"`. Then implement them.
   Verify: `pytest proxy/tests/test_prompt_log.py -k "flatten or last_message"` green; `ruff check` clean.
2. **Wire the writer.** Switch `extract_prompt()` to the flattener (**leave `router_helpers._first_message_content()` untouched** — it also feeds the `proxy.log` body preview) and add `current_prompt`, `current_prompt_role`, `current_prompt_truncated` to `build_entry()`/`record_exchange()`, each capped by `prompt_log.max_prompt_chars`.
   Verify: the existing writer/queue/rotation tests still pass; new tests assert the added fields, the caps and that recording stays non-blocking and non-fatal.
3. **Pin the read path.** No change to `recent_entries()`/`recent_payload()`: add a regression test asserting a stored legacy repr-style entry passes through the endpoint byte-for-byte unchanged (raw display, as today).
4. **UI.** In `proxy/templates/view_logs.html` add the `Current message` column immediately after the first-message column (role label + `PROMPT_PREVIEW_CHARS` cap + full text in `title`, both via `escapeHtml`), reusing the existing preview/tooltip convention.
   Verify: an endpoint/page test asserts the new `<th>`; a rendering assertion shows no `{'type':` fragment for a new-style entry and a placeholder for a non-text block.
5. **Docs.** `proxy/README.md` § *Prompt Log (`prompt-log.jsonl`)*: new fields in the table, the text-extraction rule, the second column, and the explicit "readable only for entries recorded after this change" limitation; `README.md` prompt-log bullet.
6. **Gate.** Full suite via `/skill:test`, then commit in build → test → commit order and stage the item `in_review`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] For a request whose first non-system message content is a content-block list (e.g. `[{"type":"text","text":"…"}]`), `GET /logs/prompt-log` returns prose text for the first-message field — never a Python/JSON repr — and the `/logs` Prompt Log table shows no `{'type':` fragment for any entry recorded after this change. Verified by a pytest test on the payload plus a UI assertion.
- [ ] The Prompt Log table has a second `Current message` column rendering the readable text of the request's **last non-system** message, labelled with that message's role, with the same preview cap and hover-full-text behaviour as the first-message column.
- [ ] New JSONL entries carry both prompts (existing `prompt` field semantics unchanged; new field(s) for the current message plus its role and truncation flag), each capped by `prompt_log.max_prompt_chars`; recording remains non-blocking, bounded and never fatal (existing writer contract and its tests unchanged).
- [ ] Non-text content blocks (image, tool result, etc.) are rendered as short placeholders (e.g. `<image>`, `<tool_result:1234 chars>`) rather than dropped silently or dumped raw; a message with no text blocks renders exactly one placeholder. A trailing `role: "system"` message is never selected or displayed.
- [ ] The read path is unchanged in cost and shape: no repr/JSON decoding of stored entries, no additional file reads, and the existing bounded window (`max_entries`) is preserved — asserted by a test that a legacy repr-style entry still round-trips through the endpoint unchanged (it renders raw, exactly as today).
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries (`README.md` prompt-log bullet and `proxy/README.md` § *Prompt Log*: field table gains the new fields, the tab description gains the second column and the text-extraction rule, and the "readable only for new entries" limitation is stated).
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes (via the test skill / `run_tests.py`), with `ruff` clean on changed files.

## Impact

Operators can read at a glance what each proxy request actually asked — both the session's opening prompt and the message just submitted — instead of decoding a dumped Python data structure.

## Constraints

- Implement in this repo (`llm-manager`, FastAPI app under `proxy/`), on `dev`; pushes only to `dev` (release promotes `dev` → `main`).
- **Do not change the shared `router_helpers._first_message_content()` behaviour** — it also feeds the `proxy.log` body preview (80-char cap, different redaction/display contract). Flattening belongs in the prompt-log path (a prompt-log-scoped helper, or a flatten step applied in `prompt_log.py`).
- System-prompt content must stay out of the log and the UI — the "first non-system message" and last-message rules must never surface a `role: "system"` message. If the *last* message is a system message (rare, e.g. a trailing steering message), it must be skipped rather than displayed.
- Preserve the writer's existing contract: one complete line written once, bounded queue, bounded file growth, bounded tail reads, append failures counted and never raised into the request path.
- No schema-breaking change: old entries must keep working with the new reader (field-by-field, tolerant of missing new fields), and old readers are not a concern (single deployable).
- **Legacy entries are out of scope (operator decision, D2).** Do not add read-time repr/JSON decoding of stored `prompt` values, and do not rewrite `prompt-log.jsonl*`. Older rows may keep showing the raw repr until they age out — that is accepted.
- Follow existing Web UI conventions in `view_logs.html` (CSS variables, `escapeHtml`, table classes `.prompt-log-table`, preview constants).
- Out of scope: new prompt-log features beyond these two columns (search/filter, export, token counts, embeddings/TTS recording, retention changes).

## Risks & assumptions

- **R1 — Cost on the read/write path.** Flattening happens once per request at record time and per rendered entry at read time, inside the existing bounded window (`max_entries`, default 500); no whole-file work and no extra file reads. Prompts are already capped at 2000 chars.
- **R2 — "Last non-system message" is often a tool result in agent traffic.** The column may frequently show tool output rather than a fresh user instruction; the role label makes that explicit and is the agreed presentation (D1).
- **R3 — Mixed readability during transition.** Entries written before this change keep the repr display (D2: only new entries are fixed), so the tab will show both styles side by side until old entries age out of the 500-entry window / rotation. Accepted; documented in `proxy/README.md`.
- **R4 — Duplicate/coalesced requests** keep producing one entry each (existing contract); both entries will carry the same current-message text.
- **R5 — Scope creep.** Search/filtering, column sorting, legacy back-fill and prompt-log retention changes are neighbouring ideas — record them as linked work items rather than absorbing them here (`LP-0MW3GU0JO008XOUF` already covers retention).
- **A1 —** "Content of the current message" means the request's last **non-system** message in the payload, not the proxy's *response* (operator answer, D1).
- **A2 —** The UI keeps its current 240-char preview + tooltip convention for both columns rather than introducing full-text expansion.
- **A3 —** Non-text blocks are represented by placeholders; a message with only non-text blocks shows placeholders only (operator answer, D3).

## Decisions recorded during intake

- **D1 — "The current message" = the last non-system message in the request payload, labelled with its role.** Operator answer (2026-11-17), interactive intake round. Rejected: last message regardless of role (can surface a trailing system/steering message); last `role: "user"` only (hides tool-result turns).
- **D2 — Only new entries get readable text; legacy entries are not decoded.** Operator answer (2026-11-17). Rejected: read-time decoding of stored repr strings (measured feasible — 100 % of the 15 787 truncated entries remained parseable — but not wanted); rewriting the existing file.
- **D3 — Non-text content blocks render as short placeholders** (`<image>`, `<tool_result:1234 chars>`). Operator answer (2026-11-17). Rejected: dropping them silently; dumping them raw.
- **D4 — The current-message column is additive** and sits immediately after the first-message column. Source: the item description ("Add a second column that adds the content of the current message").

## Key Files

- `proxy/proxy/prompt_log.py` — add a content-block text flattener (text parts concatenated, non-text parts as placeholders), a last-non-system-message extractor, and the new entry fields. **No** changes to legacy decode behaviour in `recent_entries`/`recent_payload`.
- `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py` — reuse `_first_message_content()`'s message-selection policy; **read-only** for this change (shared with the `proxy.log` body preview).
- `proxy/proxy/session_recorder.py` — **reuse candidate**: `_extract_message_text()` already flattens `type: "text"` content parts for the session-dropdown preview; generalise it (or share a helper with it) rather than duplicating the logic.
- `proxy/templates/view_logs.html` — add the `Current message` column, render both previews as text, keep `PROMPT_PREVIEW_CHARS`/tooltip/`escapeHtml` conventions and the `.prompt-log-table` styles.
- `proxy/tests/test_prompt_log.py` — unit tests: flattener (string / one block / many blocks / mixed blocks / empty), last-non-system-message selection (incl. trailing system message skipped), entry shape and caps, endpoint payload, a legacy repr entry passing through unchanged, and a `/logs` page assertion for the new column.
- `proxy/README.md` — § *Prompt Log (`prompt-log.jsonl`)*: new fields in the table, the text-extraction rule, the second column.
- `README.md` — the prompt-log bullet in the Web UI feature list.

## Related work

- **Prompt log: track the first message of each proxy request (time, prompt, session ID, routed model) in a log, with a Web UI tab (LP-0MVP79OBP002G6Z1)** — completed; built the log, the endpoint and the tab this item improves.

Source: interactive intake reply. Recorded as D2; supersedes the draft's recommended read-time decoding, and the corresponding AC/constraint/risk entries were updated.

## Goal

Produce a **proposal** (no implementation without explicit producer approval) for separating audit/bulk traffic from interactive user traffic at the shared local gate.

**Discovered from:** LP-0MVO8H7VQ003B12I. Rec 5 of the root-cause analysis. **This item must not change code, config or the running proxy.**

## Why it matters (measured, certified window 2026-11-06 14:15:50 → 2026-11-08 00:00)

- **20 of the 60** `prefill_deadline` events are audit sessions (`audit-*`), with 44k–103k prompts; 11 audit events are attributed capacity and 9 predicted-warmth.
- Audit is excluded from the (b2) user-class criterion, **but not from its cause**: audit prefills occupy the shared gate and the second slot, and the measured cold rate swings **235–295 tok/s (contended) vs 530–770 tok/s (best case)**.
- Audits raise the occupancy class (9/60, 15 %, and under-counted while `/slots` times out), i.e. they make *user* events miss even though their own events are not counted.

## Scope

**In:** a written proposal in `docs/dev/` (or an appendix to the existing prefill/admission docs) covering options, costs and the decision criteria.

**Out:** any implementation, config change, deployment or proxy restart. Implementation happens only in a follow-up item created **after** producer approval.

## Options the proposal must cost

1. **Audit remote-only** (or audit-on-a-different-provider): zero local audit load; cost = remote tokens/latency.
2. **Idle-gated local access for audits**: local only when the pool has been idle ≥ N s; needs a measured N.
3. **Priority-weighted gate**: user `high`/`medium` pre-empts queued audit prefills; needs the priority plumbing already present (LP-0MW0KZV5H004Z4UI).
4. **Per-class deadline**: audits get a shorter local deadline (e.g. 60 s) and fall back sooner.
5. **Do nothing** — with the measured cost stated.

For each: expected effect on the user-class rate, on local coverage/utilisation, on remote spend, and the risk.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Proposal written.** A document states each option, its mechanism, the measured evidence it rests on, expected effect on the user-class combined rate (baseline 2.223/h; target ≤ 0.5/h), local coverage, and remote cost. It names a recommendation and the decision criteria.
- **AC2 — No implementation.** The item changes **no** source, config or runtime state; git diff is empty apart from the proposal document (or the doc lives in the work item description if a doc is premature). No proxy restart is performed by this item.
- **AC3 — Impact model reproducible.** The projected numbers come from a stated, reproducible computation over the certified window dataset (`/tmp/ac3-window-2026-11-06.json`, recorded on LP-0MVO8H7VQ003B12I) — e.g. "remove audit events → X user events remain, Y/h", with the command/analysis recorded.
- **AC4 — Producer approval gate.** `needsProducerReview` is set on creation; the item advances only when the producer records approval (a comment naming the chosen option). Until then it stays `idea`/`intake_complete` and dispatchable-for-proposal only.
- **AC5 — Follow-up on approval.** On approval, create the implementation item (issue type `feature`, high) carrying: the restart AC (proxy restarted via `/skill:start-proxy --restart` with PID/HEAD/`/health` evidence), the dated-title re-anchor AC, and the impact measurement. Link it here with `related`/`depends-on` as appropriate.
- **AC6 — Proxy restart AC (deferred, not waived).** This item performs no restart. The restart it is accountable for is the one in the approved follow-up: that follow-up must restart the proxy and record old/new PID, start time, deployed HEAD and `/health` before its impact measurement. If the producer rejects the proposal, state explicitly that no restart is owed and close.
- **AC7 — Dated titles.** The dated-title re-anchor (`\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}` in open titles) is owed by the approved follow-up's restart; this item records that obligation and, on rejection, notes that no re-anchor is triggered.

## Relationship

- Related: LP-0MW0KZUJP0019SLS (serialise audits at the shared local resource), LP-0MW0KZV5H004Z4UI (batch work must send a priority header so interactive sessions are protected), LP-0MVVEQW5Y00962T2 (early-released local dispatch starvation).

Running `wl doctor upgrade` rewrites the committed `.githooks/pre-push`, `.githooks/post-merge` and `.githooks/post-rewrite` from this repo's committed v4/v2 templates to the ContextHub wl CLI's canonical v3/v1 templates (`PRE_PUSH_HOOK_CONTENT`). The downgrade turns the working tree red and would also be a regression if committed.

## Impact
- Discovered while auditing LP-0MW305AJ80085AEK: `wl doctor upgrade` (run to clear a schemaVersion error) left the three hooks dirty, so the full suite failed on `tests/test_git_hooks.py::test_missing_runner_fails_closed_on_dev_push` and the audit's F3 triage created a false-positive test-failure item (LP-0MWC0K2DD0073YML, since closed).
- Any dev push from the dirty checkout would trip the repo's own pushed-commit dirty-tree guard.

# Grant `tailscale serve` privileges so Grafana is reachable on the tailnet

## Why

`scripts/deploy_grafana.sh` publishes Grafana on the tailnet with
`tailscale serve --bg --tcp=3000`. On this host that call is refused:

```
sending serve config: Access denied: serve config denied
Use 'sudo tailscale set --operator=rgardler'.
```

`tailscaled` only accepts serve configuration from root or from the configured
**operator**. The agent runs as `rgardler`, there is no passwordless sudo, and
`tailscale serve status` reports `No serve config`. The script therefore
degrades to loopback-only with a warning — the behaviour the parent epic's
AC 4 explicitly specifies — and the dashboard is reachable at
`http://127.0.0.1:3000` but not at `http://100.79.231.101:3000`.

## What is needed (operator action — requires sudo)

Run **one** of:

```
sudo tailscale set --operator=rgardler     # preferred: no root needed afterwards
```

or make the serve call itself privileged, then:

```
tailscale serve --bg --tcp=3000 http://127.0.0.1:3000
tailscale serve status                      # expect a :3000 TCP forwarder
curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' http://100.79.231.101:3000/api/health
```

## Acceptance criteria

1. `sudo tailscale set --operator=rgardler` has been run (or serve config is otherwise permitted for `rgardler`), so `tailscale serve --bg --tcp=3000 http://127.0.0.1:3000` succeeds without sudo.
2. `tailscale serve status` shows a `:3000` TCP forwarder to `http://127.0.0.1:3000`.
3. `http://100.79.231.101:3000/api/health` reports `"database": "ok"` from the tailnet address.
4. `scripts/deploy_grafana.sh` re-run reports `published on the tailnet via tailscale serve --tcp=3000` (no degradation warning) and `--check` still exits `0`.
5. `ss -tln` still shows Grafana bound to `127.0.0.1:3000` only — the tailnet path is Tailscale's listener, not a widened bind.

## Notes

- This item is operator-gated: an agent cannot supply the sudo password. It is
  not a code defect — the script already implements the documented degradation
  path correctly.
- No secret is involved: the admin password stays in
  `~/.config/grafana/admin.pass` (`0600`).

## Impact

Once the serve privilege is granted, the memory dashboard is reachable from any
device on the tailnet instead of only from this host's loopback.


## Origin

Discovered during work on LP-0MWCQKN3C0034R6Z (epic LP-0MVWUTC2J006PKBJ). Not a blocker: the epic's AC 4 explicitly specifies loopback-only degradation when `tailscale serve` is unavailable, and it is unavailable to this non-privileged account. This item records the privileged step needed to *also* expose the dashboard on the tailnet.

# Usage report: per-model provider status table with next-check time

## Goal (user story)

As a proxy operator reading the daily usage report, I want a table immediately
after the performance-metrics scorecard showing the **current routing status of
every provider entry in every model chain, and when that status will next be
checked or re-evaluated**, so that a silently deadlocked provider is visible in
the report the morning it happens instead of being found by hand weeks later.

## Problem

The report can say *how often* the chain fell back and to where, but it cannot
answer the question the operator actually asks when fallback is high: **"which
provider is unavailable right now, why, and when does that change?"** The
statuses that suppress a provider are already computed by the resolver but
never surfaced:

| Gate (evaluated in this order, `proxy/proxy/provider.py`) | Line | Suppresses the entry for |
|---|---|---|
| `usage_limit_account` (same account already exhausted this request) | ~11533 | the rest of that request |
| `quota_exhausted` / `dispatch_on_balance` (proactive quota snapshot) | ~11546 | until the blocking quota window resets |
| `usage_limit_reset_pending` (persisted account quarantine) | ~11560 | until `reset_at` (minutes → **weeks**) |
| `quota_hard_stop` | ~11606 | until the monthly window resets |
| `provider_cooldown` | ~11628 | 30 s – 300 s |
| `outside its available_times` | ~11647 | until the next window edge |

The gap is not theoretical. On 2026-11-12 05:46:05 `opencode-go` returned HTTP
402 `Insufficient balance`; the proxy recorded a `balance_exhaustion`
quarantine bounded by the **monthly plan** reset — **2026-11-23 08:45:55** —
and then skipped the entry on every request for eleven days. Nothing in the
report showed it: every nightly run looked normal, the account simply never
appeared, and the deadlock was only found by reading `proxy-state.json` by
hand and grepping `usage_limit_reset_pending` out of the live log. A single
table with `opencode-go | usage_limit_reset_pending | next checked
2026-11-23 08:45` would have made it obvious on the first morning.

Visibility is also the cheaper alternative to automating early quarantine
release: the operator can see that a top-up will not be picked up until the
plan window rolls over, and act (or not) deliberately.

## Scope

In scope (usage-report skill only — `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/`):

- a new `## Provider status` table rendered **immediately after** the
  `## Performance metrics summary` scorecard table (`scripts/reporting.py`,
  currently line ~1384) and **before** `## Performance metric details`
  (line ~1481);
- a new deterministic module (suggested `scripts/provider_status.py`) that
  derives the rows; it must not re-implement the resolver's gate semantics —
  see *Design notes*;
- an additive `--json` block (`provider_status`);
- tests (unit + fixture-rendered) and the skill's `SKILL.md` / `REFERENCE.md`
  updates.

Out of scope:

- changing any proxy routing behaviour, quarantine duration or probe cadence
  (this item is observational only — it must not alter what the proxy does);
- adding a network call to the proxy, Prometheus or any other live service;
- alerting/paging on status (the report row is the deliverable).

## Table shape

One table, ordered by model chain (config order) then by chain position, so
each model's fallback sequence reads top-down:

| Model | # | Provider entry | Status | Detail | Next check |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| plan | 1 | local-qwen3 | eligible | — | next request |
| plan | 2 | opencode-go-3 | quota_exhausted | monthly 100.0 %, resets in 10.3 h | 2026-11-17 10:07 |
| plan | 3 | opencode-go-2 | quota_exhausted | monthly 100.0 %, resets in 13 days | 2026-11-30 00:05 |
| plan | 4 | opencode-go | usage_limit_reset_pending | balance exhaustion, window unknown | 2026-11-23 08:45 |
| plan | 5 | munitoai-free | usage_limit_reset_pending | window unknown | 2026-11-17 00:02 |
| plan | 6 | munitoai | outside available_times | next window 10:00–23:00 UTC | 2026-11-17 10:00 |
| plan | 7 | deepseek-flash | outside available_times | next window 10:00–00:00 UTC | 2026-11-17 10:00 |

`Status` is the **first suppressing gate** the resolver would hit (the order
above), or `eligible` when none does. `Detail` carries the gate's own evidence
(quota window + percent, quarantine window + reason, cooldown key and
remaining seconds, or the window being waited for). `Next check` is the
instant the suppression is expected to lift, or the next point at which the
proxy will re-evaluate it — defined in the next section so the column is never
ambiguous.

An `Events in window` column (skip count per entry, derived from the existing
`Skipping provider=` parse) is optional; add it only if it costs no extra log
pass.

## Semantics of `Next check`

The column must state *how* it was derived, because three different mechanisms
answer "when next":

| Status | `Next check` | Basis |
|---|---|---|
| `eligible` | `next request` | the resolver's gate checks run per request; nothing is pending |
| `provider_cooldown` | cooldown expiry instant | `provider_unavailable_until` in the provider state file |
| `usage_limit_reset_pending` (hard / window-derived) | quarantine `reset_at` | `usage_reset_at` in the state file; revalidated from the next quota poll, so the instant is the *earliest* lift, not a guarantee |
| `usage_limit_reset_pending` (soft / guessed) | `now + min(probe interval, reset_at)` | the self-healing probe cadence (`_USAGE_LIMIT_PROBE_INTERVAL_SECONDS`, 300 s) is what actually re-checks these |
| `quota_exhausted` / `quota_hard_stop` | the blocking window's `resetsAt` | the last `quota poll ok` line for that account (`seconds_to_reset`) |
| `outside available_times` | the next window edge in UTC | `available_times` from `proxy/config.yaml`, including overnight wraparound (e.g. `22:00-02:00`) |
| any status with no usable evidence | `unknown` | never a fabricated instant |

## Design notes and assumptions

**Data sources (all local files / already-parsed log lines — no network call):**

1. `proxy/config.yaml` — the model chains, entry order, `available_times`,
   `use_balance`, `api_key_env`, `quota_poll_interval_seconds`.
2. `proxy/provider-state.json` — `provider_unavailable_until` (cooldowns) and
   `usage_reset_at` (account quarantines). Path is overridable by
   `LLAMA_PROXY_PROVIDER_STATE_FILE` (`proxy/proxy/provider.py:296`); the
   analyser must honour that environment variable and treat a missing file as
   "no pending suppression", not an error.
3. The **last** `quota poll ok account=...` line in the analysis window per
   account — the only persisted view of the in-process quota snapshot. Poll
   cadence is `quota_poll_interval_seconds` (900 s), so a window shorter than
   that may legitimately have none.

**Single source of truth (hard requirement).** The gate order and the
reason strings must not be duplicated as prose in the report module. Either
import the constants from `proxy/provider.py` (the skill already imports
`MEASURED_CACHE_DEFICIT_REASON` this way — see the capacity-signals section of
`SKILL.md`, including the PEP 420 namespace-package caveat it documents), or
add a small canonical `GATE_ORDER` tuple there that both the resolver and the
analyser consume. A test must fail if the two orders diverge.

**Assumption A1 — row granularity.** "Each model" is read as *each model chain
(`plan`, `author`, `code`, …) × each provider entry in it*, because the entry
is the unit the gates act on and the chain position is what makes a dead entry
fatal. `opencode-go` therefore appears once per chain it belongs to. If the
operator prefers one row per distinct entry with a `Model chains` column
instead, that is a rendering change only — the derivation is identical.

**Assumption A2 — reference instant.** All relative figures are computed
against the report window's end (the analysis `--end`, default now), stated in
the section's intro sentence, so a re-run over an old window reproduces the
same table rather than silently using wall-clock time.

**Assumption A3 — live-state caveat.** `provider-state.json` and the last
quota poll are point-in-time snapshots, not window aggregates. The section
intro must say so in one sentence: the table describes the state at report
generation, not the state during the window. This is the same honesty
discipline the report already applies to the GPU row and the engine
cross-check.

**Assumption A4 — local entries.** `local-qwen3` has no endpoint and no quota
account. It is rendered with `eligible` and `next request`, or with the
existing local-route cooldown reason when one is recorded — it must not be
dropped from the table, because a reader comparing chains needs the whole
sequence.

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1** — `report.md` contains `## Provider status` immediately after the
  `## Performance metrics summary` table and before `## Performance metric
  details`. A test asserts the section order, not just presence.
- **AC2** — The table has one row per (model chain, provider entry) in
  `proxy/config.yaml` order and chain order, and a test asserts the row count
  and order equal the config's for a fixture config.
- **AC3** — `Status` is the *first* suppressing gate in the resolver's order;
  a unit test covers an entry suppressed by two mechanisms simultaneously
  (e.g. `usage_limit_reset_pending` and `provider_cooldown`) and asserts the
  earlier gate wins.
- **AC4** — `Next check` is derived per the semantics table, with unit tests
  for: cooldown expiry, hard quarantine `reset_at`, soft/guessed quarantine
  capped at the probe interval, quota window reset from the last
  `quota poll ok` line, an `available_times` window later the same UTC day,
  and an overnight window that wraps past midnight.
- **AC5** — The reproduction from this item's *Problem* section renders as
  `opencode-go | usage_limit_reset_pending | 2026-11-23 08:45` from a fixture
  built on the 2026-11-12 state file — i.e. the incident is visible.
- **AC6** — Degradation is named, never fabricated: with a missing state file,
  no `quota poll ok` line, an unparseable `available_times` entry, or an
  unknown status string, the cell reads `unknown` and the run still exits 0.
  A test covers each of the four.
- **AC7** — `--json` carries an additive `provider_status` block with the same
  rows (`model`, `position`, `entry`, `status`, `detail`, `next_check`,
  `next_check_basis`) and no existing key changes. A test asserts the Markdown
  table and the JSON rows agree.
- **AC8** — Gate order and reason strings have a single source of truth: a
  test fails if `provider_status`'s gate order or a reason string diverges from
  the proxy resolver's.
- **AC9** — No network call is added: a test asserts the module performs no
  HTTP request (the skill's `tests/conftest.py` network seam already blocks one,
  so the test proves it is never attempted) and the 05:00 cron line is
  unchanged.
- **AC10** — An empty window (no logs) still renders a valid table from config
  + state alone, with `unknown` where log evidence is needed, and the 05:00
  cron exits 0.
- **AC11** — `SKILL.md` gains a `## Provider status` section (what the columns
  mean, the `Next check` semantics table, the live-state caveat) and
  `REFERENCE.md` documents the data sources and the `--json` schema; both are
  reviewed against the rendered output in the same change.
- **AC12** — No proxy behaviour change: the diff touches only
  `.pi/skills/proxy-usage-analysis/` (plus, at most, one extracted constant in
  `proxy/proxy/provider.py` for AC8) and the full test suite passes.

## Traceability

- Discovered while root-causing the 2026-11-16 `opencode-go` deadlock (HTTP 402
  `Insufficient balance` → `balance_exhaustion` quarantine until the monthly
  plan reset 2026-11-23, skipped on every request for eleven days).
  `discovered-from` that investigation; no upstream work item exists for it.
- Related: LP-0MW0FU5Z6006A4P3 (performance metrics scorecard — the table this
  section follows), LP-0MVN4LCQJ0034S5S and LP-0MW2SQNHJ0044PV6 (usage-report
  feature precedent: summary table + detail section + honest degradation),
  LP-0MVU8O4EL005IYP9 (Local capacity signals — the shared-derivation and
  named-unavailability pattern to follow), LP-0MW46PAU4006SK7Z /
  LP-0MW46PBWL008T317 (`use_balance` and balance exhaustion — the semantics the
  `Status`/`Detail` columns must report), LP-0MUQTCMW2001VXH8 (self-healing
  probe cadence that defines the soft-quarantine `Next check`).
- Deliberately **not** done here: automating early release of a balance
  quarantine. This item only makes the state visible.

## Impact

The operator can see, in the daily report, which provider is unavailable, why,
and the exact moment it will be re-checked — so an eleven-day silent deadlock
is a single glance instead of weeks of unnoticed fallback.

## Goal

The post-acceptance eviction event that the residual analyser counts still reports the umbrella reason `no_progress_watchdog` for pre-deadline early aborts, even though the sweep already computes the distinct reason. The reason-rate criterion the producer agreed for AC3 (LP-0MVO8H7VQ003B12I, option **b2**) therefore counts a class by label rather than by behaviour, and a relabelling can be mistaken for a fix.

**Discovered from:** LP-0MVO8H7VQ003B12I (AC3 gating re-check, 2026-11-17).

## Evidence (2026-11-17, window `2026-11-16T15:20:47Z` → `13:30:00Z`, group-2 tree `79f53ac1a`)

`e5af94f75` (**LP-0MW8VOKB9002W2C1**, *measured lease extension and pre-deadline early abort*) introduced a distinct release reason and wires it into `lease_released` only:

```
03:37:13  lease_extended_during_prefill … progress=None alive=False in_flight=True reason=in_flight
03:37:18  WARNING lease_released … reason=prefill_eta_exceeded elapsed_s=15.5 stalled_for_s=15.5
03:37:18  ERROR   local_eviction … reason=tenancy_lease_expired
03:37:18  ERROR   local_eviction_after_acceptance … reason=no_progress_watchdog estimated_tokens=7550 new_tokens=7550 eta_prefill_s=7.5 elapsed_s=15.5
```

In-window log counts: `lease_released reason=prefill_eta_exceeded` **208**, `local_eviction_after_acceptance reason=no_progress_watchdog` **163**, and **zero** `local_eviction_after_acceptance reason=prefill_eta_exceeded`.

Code path:
- `proxy/proxy/router_helpers.py` — the sweep computes `_watchdog_reason(srv, record)` (`prefill_eta_exceeded` / `prefill_stalled` / `prefill_max_exceeded`, falling back to `no_progress_watchdog`) and uses it for the `lease_released` line;
- the deferred release path then calls `_emit_eviction_after_acceptance(srv, session_key, "no_progress_watchdog", released_record, …)` with the literal umbrella label, and that is the line `proxy/scripts/analyse_prefill_deadline_residual.py` counts for its per-reason attribution.

Measured effect on the residual (orientation only, same analyser version): group-1 window 4 `no_progress_watchdog` (p50 `elapsed_s` 187.3 s) vs the 2026-11-16/17 partial window 163 (user 154, p50 19.75 s). The counted reasons (`prefill_deadline` + `measured_cache_deficit`) fell to 0.181 user events/h while total user-class stall across all reasons rose from 60.57 to 246.48 s/h.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 — Distinct reason propagated.** `local_eviction_after_acceptance` reports the same distinct reason the sweep computed (`prefill_eta_exceeded`, `prefill_stalled`, `prefill_max_exceeded`), falling back to `no_progress_watchdog` only when no distinct reason applies; a hermetic test pins that the after-acceptance reason equals the `lease_released` reason for the same release.
- **AC2 — Analyser counts the distinct reason.** `analyse_prefill_deadline_residual.py` reports the distinct reasons in its per-reason split and attribution (no behaviour change to the released reasons themselves); the JSON schema stays additive.
- **AC3 — Parser compatibility.** Every existing key on the line keeps its position (the reason value is the only change); the deployed-parser contract in `docs/dev/` is updated and any reason allow-list in tests/docs is extended.

## Problem statement

The first proxy-initiated `/slots` poll after a proxy restart can fire
*before* child-port discovery has succeeded, so it takes the router-port
fallback path: it logs a `slots_child_port_unavailable` WARNING
(`model=Qwen3`, `source=log_signal`), increments
`llama_slots_child_port_fallbacks_total{reason="no_child_port_router_mode"}`
and traverses the router (`:8080`) instead of the model child port.

Consequence: every 24 h post-restart verification window on this surface
starts with a guaranteed chat-model fallback, which fails a zero-tolerance
"chat-model fallback delta == 0" acceptance criterion even when
steady-state operation is clean.

## Evidence (measured, LP-0MVP7HX2S008IU57 window 2026-11-16T15:20:47Z → 2026-11-17T15:20:47Z)

The window is anchored to the proxy restart (`pid 3720326`, `lstart`
2026-11-16T15:20:47Z), so the process-lifetime counter delta *is* the window
delta. In `proxy.log.2026-11-16_15`, immediately after the boot sequence
(`Started TTS server`, `death capture: armed`, `Slot occupancy sampler
started (interval 10.0s)`):

```text
2026-11-16 15:20:51,411 - WARNING - slots_child_port_unavailable: no model child port discovered for model=Qwen3 (source=log_signal); falling back to router port 8080 — every proxy-initiated /slots poll will traverse t...
2026-11-16 15:20:51,435 - WARNING - llama-server --version returned 127
2026-11-16 15:20:51,560 - INFO - Adopted running llama-server (model=router parallel=1 router_mode=True); preserving warm prompt cache
```

- Only **one** `Starting LLama Proxy Server` marker in the whole window
  (15:20:49.786, the anchor process's own boot) ⇒ no in-window restart.
- `llama_slots_child_port_fallbacks_total{reason="no_child_port_router_mode"}`
  = **1.0** for a process that started at the window start.
- Exactly **one** `slots_child_port_unavailable` line in the window, at
  window start **+4.4 s**; **zero** for the remaining 23 h 59 m 56 s.
- The same transient is visible in the earlier LP-0MVVLKPBM007F6U6 window
  (3 × `model=Qwen3`, each one within 3 s of a restart) — i.e. it is
  restart-correlated, not busy-child-correlated.

## Desired change

Make the boot-time slot poll child-port-aware: either

1. retry/defer the first slot poll until child-port discovery has resolved
   (bounded backoff), or
2. mark the poll as a boot transient so the fallback counter / WARNING are
   not incremented before discovery has had a chance to succeed.

The zero-tolerance signal (`llama_slots_child_port_fallbacks_total` + the
`slots_child_port_unavailable` WARNING) must stay usable as a *regression*
signal — a boot-time increment makes a clean 24 h window indistinguishable
from one real discovery regression.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1** — After a proxy restart, the first proxy-initiated `/slots` poll
  does not increment `llama_slots_child_port_fallbacks_total{reason="no_child_port_router_mode"}`
  and does not emit `slots_child_port_unavailable` when the model child port
  becomes discoverable within the boot window.
- **AC2** — A genuine discovery regression (child port never discoverable)
  still increments the counter and emits the WARNING; covered by a test.
- **AC3** — Reproduced by a test: boot sequence with a not-yet-ready child
  port ⇒ no fallback counter increment; child port never ready ⇒ counter
  increments once per throttled interval.
- **AC4** — All related documentation is updated to reflect the change.
- **AC5** — Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Impact

A restarted proxy no longer looks like it had a child-port discovery
regression on its very first slot poll, so a clean 24 h window can pass the
zero-tolerance fallback check.
